literal: coffee (the source of the English word)
usage: The word for coffee in Modern Standard Arabic, and the origin of the English word by way of Turkish kahve. It is a feminine noun. The q is pronounced in MSA, while most dialects soften it, which is why you also hear ahwa and gahwa.

variants.label: ordering one, to a man
variants.english: I would like a coffee, please
variants.note: The polite way to order in MSA.

variants.label: a cup of coffee
variants.note: finjan is the small cup coffee is served in.

variants.label: Arabic coffee
variants.note: The light, cardamom-spiced coffee of the Gulf and the Levant.

variants.label: without sugar
variants.note: Say this when ordering; sugar is often added while brewing.

variants.label: with milk
variants.note: Use to ask for milk in it.

examples.english: Do you want coffee or tea?
